title: Localization preserves universal injectivity
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $T\subseteq S$ a multiplicative subset, and $u:M\to M'$ a map of $S$-modules. Suppose $u$ is universally injective as an $R$-module map, that is, $L\otimes_R M\to L\otimes_R M'$ is injective for every $R$-module $L$. Then the localized map $T^{-1}u:T^{-1}M\to T^{-1}M'$ is universally injective as an $R$-module map. Localization is [def-weil-pbc-module-localization].

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary $R$-module $L$ and write $v=1_L\otimes_R u:L\otimes_R M\to L\otimes_R M'$. The hypothesis that $u$ is universally injective says exactly that $v$ is injective. Give $L\otimes_R M$ and $L\otimes_R M'$ their natural $S$-module structures through the second tensor factors; then $v$ is $S$-linear because $u$ is $S$-linear.

source.place: Tag 05CM, lemma-universally-injective-localize, part (1), first sentence and the definition of universal injectivity

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] with base ring $R$, algebra $S$, multiplicative subset $T$, first $S$-module $M$ (respectively $M'$), and second $R$-module $L$. Its explicit fraction formula, followed by the symmetry of tensor factors, gives isomorphisms $\theta_M:T^{-1}(L\otimes_R M)\xrightarrow{\sim}L\otimes_R T^{-1}M$ and $\theta_{M'}:T^{-1}(L\otimes_R M')\xrightarrow{\sim}L\otimes_R T^{-1}M'$, sending $(l\otimes m)/t$ to $l\otimes(m/t)$. On each pure fraction, $\theta_{M'}((T^{-1}v)((l\otimes m)/t))=l\otimes(u(m)/t)=(L\otimes_R T^{-1}u)(\theta_M((l\otimes m)/t))$. Since pure tensors and fractions generate the localized modules, this proves that the square with $T^{-1}v$ and $L\otimes_R T^{-1}u$ commutes.

source.place: Tag 00DK, lemma-tensor-localization, together with Tag 00D2, lemma-tensor-with-bimodule; explicit fraction formula and naturality

proof.text: The map $T^{-1}v$ is injective by the fraction description of localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]: if $(T^{-1}v)(x/t)=v(x)/t=0$, then some $s\in T$ satisfies $s\,v(x)=0$; injectivity of $v$ gives $s x=0$, hence $x/t=0$. Therefore the commutative square in Step 2 and the isomorphisms $\theta_M,\theta_{M'}$ show that $L\otimes_R T^{-1}u$ is injective. As $L$ was arbitrary, $T^{-1}u$ is universally injective over $R$.
